summary: Final client pass. iOS (ChatThreadView+Share, ShareToChatSheet+Threads, SharedObjectViews and ChatThreadView hook-ins) and web (useChatShare, threadShare, ShareThreadPicker, ShareToChatModal, Reader, useMessaging) send only the minimal share request; the server rebuilds meta and fallback text (verified by step 3 and the 79-check backend test), so no client-trusted meta. Flags: iOS picker and deliver both require threads and chat_shared_objects (deliver does nothing if either is off); web canShareToThreads fails closed and gates the picker. Failure handling: iOS deliver clears the pending share first and sends only if the thread opened with a loaded first page, otherwise drops without sending or fabricating; web pendingShareStatus drops with a toast on thread open error or 404, and sendThreadMessage now returns false on a dead socket so a toast shows rather than a silent drop. No re-queue loops: pending share is consumed once on both platforms and never re-queued. Logging: no console calls in new web files; the only iOS log is a print of a thread-list fetch error (no note text or user content). Recent-thread lists are fetched through existing authorized endpoints and capped at 10; failed loads keep existing rows. Notes: tracked __pycache__ .pyc and vitest results.json show as modified, exclude from commit. No source edits made.
